text: The Patriots continue to navigate a rough start to the season with several personnel moves aimed at shoring up their struggling offense: they've signed offensive lineman Matt Pryor from the Arizona Cardinals practice squad to bolster the unit, though they simultaneously placed guard Greg Van Roten on injured reserve due to a thigh injury, creating ongoing challenges along the line protecting Drake Maye. The quarterback himself insists his right shoulder remains fine and that his early-season struggles stem from poor decision-making rather than physical limitations, as New England ranks dead last in the NFL with just 9.7 offensive points per game through a 1-2 start. On a brighter note, wide receiver Mack Hollins earned the Week 4 NFLPA Community MVP award after hosting a Special Olympics Family Field Day for over 125 athletes and their families, showcasing the kind of community impact the team values off the field. As the Patriots prepare to face the Bills, they'll need Maye to clean up his turnovers while their patchwork offensive line—bolstered by Pryor's arrival but weakened by Van Roten's absence—provides him the time and protection necessary to reverse this alarming scoring drought.
